[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday 'copy' (b = a, like copying a value onto paper) suggests a second, separate thing. For arrays, b = a only copies the reference; a separate copy needs a new array with each element copied.
[1] misconception (M) -> AssignmentCopiesObject: wrong rule: Assigning an array reference copies the array. Right rule: b = a copies only the reference, so a and b refer to the same array; to copy, create a new array and copy each element.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> AssignmentCopiesObject: Applies the copy rule unevenly: copies element by element in one place but writes b = a in another and expects b to be independent. (here mixing in: "assigning a reference copies the object")
[3] misconception (M) -> ArrayEqualityComparesValues: wrong rule: a == b is true when a and b hold the same values. Right rule: == compares whether a and b are the same array, so a copy and its original are not ==, even with equal elements.

[0] names_the_element (N): Array copy: a second, independent array holding the same elements as the first.
[1] states_the_rule (S): To copy an array, create a new array of the same length and copy the elements one by one: double[] b = new double[N]; for (int i = 0; i < N; i++) b[i] = a[i]; (java.util.Arrays.copyOf does the same).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: new creates the second array first, then the loop copies a[0], a[1], ... in order into b[0], b[1], ...; after the loop, a and b are separate arrays with equal elements.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: after copying, b[i] == a[i] for every i, but a == b is false; after b[0] = 9, a[0] is unchanged.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: each pass of the copy loop sets one element of the new array and leaves the original unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The copy is a traversal of every index of the original.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): b = a makes an alias of the same array; a copy is a different array: changes through one are not seen through the other.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan: copy an array when the original must stay unchanged while the copy is modified (for example shuffling or sorting a copy).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> AssignmentCopiesObject: Conservation: changing the copy never changes the original, and the reverse; with an alias every change is shared.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): When an algorithm must change an array but the original is still needed, work on a copy made with new and a loop (or Arrays.copyOf).
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Assignment copies the reference, not the elements. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: b = a is used as a copy and then b is modified while a is expected to stay unchanged

b = a makes a second name for the same array (an alias); copying makes a second array: after a copy, changing b[i] leaves a[i] unchanged.
The elements are copied one at a time by a loop over every index.
